from rest_framework import viewsets, permissions
from .models import DocumentComment
from .serializers import DocumentCommentSerializer

# Route: /teams/{team_pk}/documents/{document_pk}/comments/
class NestedDocumentCommentViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    serializer_class = DocumentCommentSerializer
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]

    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        serializer.save(
            author=self.request.user,
            document_id=self.kwargs['document_pk']
        )
diagnosis: When creating a comment on a nested document route (/teams/{team_pk}/documents/{document_pk}/comments/), perform_create assigns document_id directly from URL kwargs without verifying that document_pk belongs to team_pk or that request.user belongs to team_pk. An attacker can inject unauthorized comments into confidential documents belonging to other teams.

corrected_code:
from rest_framework import viewsets, permissions
from rest_framework.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from .models import DocumentComment, TeamDocument
from .serializers import DocumentCommentSerializer

class NestedDocumentCommentViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    serializer_class = DocumentCommentSerializer
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]

    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        team_pk = self.kwargs['team_pk']
        document_pk = self.kwargs['document_pk']
        doc = get_object_or_404(TeamDocument, id=document_pk, team_id=team_pk)
        if not doc.team.members.filter(id=self.request.user.id).exists():
            raise PermissionDenied("You are not a member of the team owning this document.")
        serializer.save(author=self.request.user, document=doc)
